Self-attention smoothing and clustering of shapes

Source: R/shape_attention.R
shape_attention.Rd

Replaces each configuration by an attention-weighted average of the others in tangent coordinates, then clusters the smoothed points. The attention is the scaled dot-product attention of transformers with no trained projections: queries, keys and values are the tangent coordinates themselves, and the weights are a softmax of minus the squared distances.

Usage

shape_attention(
  X,
  K,
  perplexity = NULL,
  layers = 1L,
  alpha = 0.5,
  reduce = c("pca", "none"),
  var_explained = 0.9,
  max_dim = 10L,
  base = c("kmeans", "pam"),
  nstart = 10L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

X

Numeric array of dimension \(k \times m \times n\), with \(m\) equal to 2 or 3.

K

Number of clusters (>= 2).

perplexity

Effective number of neighbors each observation attends to. Each row's temperature is set by bisection so that \(\exp(-\sum_j a_{ij}\log a_{ij})\) equals this value. Default min(30, max(5, floor(n / (2 K)))).

layers

Number of attention layers (default 1). Weights are recomputed from the smoothed points at each layer.

alpha

Residual weight in \((0, 1]\): each layer returns \((1-\alpha) x_i + \alpha \sum_j a_{ij} x_j\). Default 0.5.

reduce

"pca" (default) works in the leading principal components of the tangent coordinates, chosen as in shape_ensemble; "none" uses all tangent coordinates.

var_explained, max_dim

PCA rule, as in shape_ensemble.

base

Clusterer applied to the smoothed points: "kmeans" (default, kmeans with nstart starts) or "pam" (shape_pam on their Euclidean distances).

nstart

Number of k-means starts (default 10).

seed

Optional integer seed. The caller's random-number stream is restored on exit.

Value

An object of class "shape_attention", a list with

cluster

Integer vector of length n, values in 1:K.

smoothed

n x d matrix of smoothed coordinates.

attention

n x n attention matrix of the first layer.

beta

Inverse temperature of each row in the first layer.

self_mass

Mean first-layer attention inside the own cluster.

dim

Number of coordinates used.

perplexity, layers, alpha, base, K

The options used.

Details

The attention matrix has zero diagonal, so each point is replaced by an average of other points; with alpha < 1 part of the point is kept, as in the residual connection of a transformer. Stacking layers with recomputed weights is the blurring mean shift of Cheng (1995), and it is also the self-attention dynamics studied by Geshkovski et al. (2023), under which points merge into clusters.

The smoothing helps when the attention mass of a point falls mostly on its own group. The returned self_mass is the average share of attention that falls inside the point's final cluster, a label-free proxy for that condition. Values near \(1/K\) mean the attention did not separate the groups.

Under a mixture of independent observations no function of the whole sample classifies a point better than the Bayes rule applied to that point alone, so the smoothing cannot remove overlap between groups; it can only reduce the loss due to estimating centers and searching partitions. In Gaussian simulations it did not beat k-means with 10 starts in any setting tried. The function is experimental.

References

Vaswani, A. et al. (2017). Attention is all you need. NeurIPS 30.

Cheng, Y. (1995). Mean shift, mode seeking, and clustering. IEEE TPAMI 17(8), 790–799.

Geshkovski, B., Letrouit, C., Polyanskiy, Y. and Rigollet, P. (2023). The emergence of clusters in self-attention dynamics. NeurIPS 36.

See also

shape_ensemble, shape_kmeans

Examples

sim <- sim_shapes3d(n = 60, sigma = 1, k = 8, seed = 1)
fit <- shape_attention(sim$X, K = 2, seed = 1)
fit
#> Shape attention clustering
#>   n = 120  K = 2  dim = 2  perplexity = 30  layers = 1  alpha = 0.5  base = kmeans 
#>   cluster sizes: 60 60 
#>   attention mass inside own cluster: 1.000 (1/K = 0.500)
table(sim$group, fit$cluster)
#>    
#>      1  2
#>   1  0 60
#>   2 60  0
